records.title: Are Mutants a Valid Substitute for Real Faults in Software Testing?
records.version: Just et al., FSE 2014; DOI 10.1145/2635868.2635929; author-hosted PDF hash recorded
records.summary: The study compares developer-fixed faults and mutants in five Java programs, controls code coverage, and reports an association. Its isolation of faulty/fixed versions is useful experimental practice.
limitations: The sampled programs and reproducible mined faults bound applicability; these results do not establish Lean transfer or turn a mutant kill into a real defect.

records.title: Are Mutation Scores Correlated with Real Fault Detection? A Large Scale Empirical Study on the Relationship Between Mutants and Real Faults
records.version: Papadakis et al., ICSE 2018; DOI 10.1145/3180155.3180183; institutional final PDF read through web; hashed author-group preprint separately identified
records.summary: Using C and Java fault datasets, this study finds weaker associations after controlling test-suite size, while high-scoring suites can still improve detection. It explicitly compares its findings with Just et al.
limitations: This is evidence to control suite size and report direct outcomes, not a Lean-specific effectiveness estimate.

Direct institutional download failed certificate verification; author-group preprint was hashed instead. Its placeholder conference typography is retained as a version difference, not treated as final typeset bytes.

records.title: Lean Language Reference: Validating a Lean Proof
records.version: 4.34.0-rc2; initially discovered through latest alias; versioned HTML separately hashed
records.summary: The manual distinguishes stored-proof replay from exported checking and trusted-statement matching. External checking retains assumptions about logic, plumbing, sandbox, shared bugs and interpretation.
limitations: Current documentation is methods context only. It does not retroactively qualify any catalog entry or prove an executable profile refines the pinned declaration judgment.
locators: Gold Standard: comparator and external checkers

records.title: Ferriprove source and readiness documentation
records.summary: The pinned CLI main function only prints a placeholder. Parser and environment code exists, but that CLI supplies no checking path. README verification claims conflict with its unfinished milestone table and the soundness document reporting no verified components.
limitations: No build or checker ran; this is a source-readiness boundary, not an observed rejection, exploit or soundness finding.
Nanoda is referenced as prior art and Lean4Lean as a proposed proof oracle; separate repository ownership cannot establish semantic independence.
locators: README.md:Relationship to Existing Work and Status

records.title: Lean4Less translation framework
records.summary: The README identifies a modification of Lean4Lean that inserts explicit transports when translating to smaller theories. This can inform a later translation question, but it shares implementation ancestry and changes the checked object/theory.
limitations: No isolated translation contract or independently validated target for this study is established. This exclusion is narrower than a claim that translation research lacks value.

search_scope: Four queries; five source groups reviewed; one pinned implementation inspection. Bounded selection, not a systematic survey or global absence result.
excluded_discoveries: Social posts, encyclopedias, course notes and Arena score pages were discovery results only; no claims rely on them.
